approachQuestion.prompt: A pattern p contains lowercase letters, ? and *. A ? matches exactly one letter; a * matches any sequence of letters, including empty. Return whether p matches the entire lowercase text s. Examples: p="a*?", s="ab" → true; p="?", s="" → false; p="**", s="" → true. Which approach is most suitable?
constraints: 0 ≤ m=p.length,n=s.length ≤ 1500; inputs are read-only. Entire text must match, not just a fragment.

options.text: Use two Boolean rows over text prefix lengths. Initially only the empty-pattern/empty-text cell is true. For each pattern character set column zero true only if it is * and the preceding row at zero is true. For j>0, a letter or ? uses the preceding diagonal when it matches; * uses preceding-row[j] OR current-row[j−1]. Swap rows.
options.feedback: A star either consumes nothing, leaving the preceding pattern, or consumes one more character while remaining available. The empty-text base must propagate through stars only.

options.text: Compute the same pattern/text prefix recurrence but retain every row in a full table.
options.feedback: This computes the correct result on the whole domain, but retains old states that future transitions never read. Removing those states preserves correctness and reduces auxiliary storage.

options.text: Make * consume exactly one letter, just like ?.
options.feedback: For p="a*", s="a", the star must consume empty, but this rejects the valid match.

options.text: Return true as soon as any prefix of s matches the entire pattern.
options.feedback: For p="a", s="ab", matching the first letter is insufficient; the entire text must match.

feedback.reason: Handle empty-prefix propagation and a self-row consuming transition for wildcard stars.
details: Allocate two arrays of n+1 Boolean entries. Initialize the empty-pattern row, then compute all m rows, including column zero and all n text columns, using the stated star or character transitions. Swap references without copying.

A star either matches empty or consumes one more text character while remaining active. A question mark consumes exactly one. Initialize empty-text columns from all-star prefixes rather than treating every pattern as matching empty.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Allocate two arrays of n+1 Boolean entries. Initialize the empty-pattern row, then compute all m rows, including column zero and all n text columns, using the stated star or character transitions. Swap references without copying. Analyze this fixed implementation. N=m+n; m,n vary independently and may be zero. Choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Array indexing and word arithmetic take constant time. No hashing, amortized containers, recursion, slicing, or input copying is used. Count all allocated work arrays and temporaries; exclude the read-only input and scalar output.
Include initialization; treat the stated dimensions as variable parameters within their bounds. Use a word per stored counter or flag, not a packed bitset.

feedback.reason: Compute every pattern/text state with two Boolean rows, including empty boundaries.
details: Initialization costs n+1; each of m rows costs n+1. Two rows of n+1 flags are live, including empty strings. There is no recursive backtracking or substring copying.
“O(m+n+1) time, O(n+1) auxiliary space”: All pattern/text prefix pairs are computed, including each row’s empty-text base.
“O((m+1)(n+1)) time, O((m+1)(n+1)) auxiliary space”: Only two text-width rows are retained, not the full prefix grid.
“O((m+1)(n+1)) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The two rows each contain n+1 Boolean entries and cannot be counted as constant workspace.
